_what: CC-LEARNING-ENGINE-L0 acceptance 3, second reference — the FSRS-4.5 COMPONENT formulas, from a different implementation than the py-fsrs trajectory.
_why_this_version: FSRS-4.5. The same test file opens by asserting FACTOR == 19/81 == 0.9^(1/DECAY) - 1 with DECAY = -0.5, which is the 4.5 forgetting curve, and its parameter vector is 17 long.
_why_a_second_source: The py-fsrs trajectory cannot reach w0, w1, w5 or w15: no sequence of whole-day reviews opens with both Again and Hard, and a Hard never occurs in it. These are per-component values, so they reach what a trajectory cannot. The published numbers are also computed at EXACT retrievability (r = 0.8), which an integer day count cannot produce -- the nearest day gives 0.79987 -- so they can only be checked against component functions, never end to end.
_grades_order: ts-fsrs iterates Grades = [Again, Hard, Good, Easy]. This engine has no Easy (D3 removed it), so the fourth entry of each row is recorded but not asserted.

next_recall_stability._call: next_recall_stability(d, s, r, grade), one (d, s, r) per grade
next_recall_stability._the_one_that_matters: index 1 is the HARD rating, so it is the only published number anywhere in this fixture set that exercises w15, the hard penalty. Index 0 is recall-stability computed with an Again rating, which no scheduler calls (an Again takes the forget path) but which is well defined and still constrains w8, w9 and w10.

next_forget_stability._call: next_forget_stability(d, s, r), same (d, s, r) rows
next_forget_stability._note: unclamped, as published. This engine additionally refuses to let a lapse raise stability; that clamp lives in fsrs_review_graded_with, not in the component, so the component stays comparable.

_rounding: ts-fsrs rounds each component to 8 decimal places with Decimal.toFixed(8) before asserting. Comparisons here allow 1e-7, which is that rounding and nothing more.
_what_is_still_NOT_covered: w0, w1 and w5 remain formula conformance rather than independent reproduction, and no fixture can change that: both py-fsrs and ts-fsrs DEFINE initial stability as w[G-1] and initial difficulty as w4 - w5*(G-3), so there is no computed number to disagree about. What a test catches there is an index off-by-one or a sign error, which is worth having and is not the same claim.
